findings.title: A failed mermaid chunk load is cached for good, so diagrams never render again until the page reloads.
findings.body:
`loadMermaid()` saves the first `import('mermaid')` promise in `mermaidPromise`. If that import rejects (a network blip, or a stale chunk after a deploy), the rejected promise stays cached. Every later call to `renderMermaidDiagrams` gets the same rejection and goes straight to the `catch` that flags every block. This happens even after the network recovers, on every README and every theme switch, until a full page reload.

Fix: clear the cache when the import fails, e.g. `mermaidPromise = import('mermaid').then(m => m.default).catch(e => { mermaidPromise = undefined; throw e; });`.

held.title: The resolution forces mermaid's URL sanitizer down to an older pinned version.
held.body:
`"mermaid/@braintree/sanitize-url": "7.0.1"` overrides the `@braintree/sanitize-url` version that mermaid declares. As far as I know, mermaid 11.x asks for `^7.1.1`, so this pins an older release that mermaid was not built against. Mermaid uses this library to clean link URLs in diagrams. These diagrams come from untrusted README content, so a downgrade can bring back URL-sanitizing bugs fixed in later 7.x releases. I could not check the yarn.lock changes or the exact changelog of each release. The PR does not explain the override, and the feature does not need it.

Fix: drop the resolution, or document why it is needed and pin a version inside mermaid's declared range.
